nodes.label: Claude Code CHANGELOG span (0.2.21 -> 2.1.258)
nodes.rationale: The official anthropics/claude-code CHANGELOG at tag v2.1.258 is a single reverse-chronological file with 383 version headings, oldest 0.2.21 (fuzzy matching for /commands) and newest 2.1.258. Entries are one-line bullets classified as Added / Fixed / Changed / Improved / Removed, with `[VSCode]`, `[IDE]`, `[SDK]` and `Windows:` platform prefixes.

nodes.label: Model lineup evolution
nodes.rationale: Model releases anchor the changelog's major versions: Sonnet 4 and Opus 4 at 1.0.0 (GA), Opus 4.1 at 1.0.69, Haiku 4.5 at 2.0.17, Opus 4.5 at 2.0.51, Opus 4.6 at 2.1.32, Sonnet 4.6 at 2.1.45, Opus 4.7 at 2.1.111, Opus 4.8 at 2.1.154, Fable 5 at 2.1.170, Sonnet 5 at 2.1.197, Opus 5 at 2.1.219, Fable 5.1 at 2.1.257. Older models are retired rather than kept: 2.1.68 removed Opus 4 and 4.1 from the first-party API and auto-moved pinned users to Opus 4.6.

nodes.label: Fable 5.1 becomes the default Fable model
nodes.rationale: 2.1.257 added Claude Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`) as the default Fable model with a 1M context window and $10/$50 per Mtok pricing plus $0.25/Mtok cache reads. The same release kept the `fable` and `best` aliases resolving to Fable 5 inside Claude apps gateway sessions, because gateways not yet configured for 5.1 reject it; users pick 5.1 explicitly in `/model`.

nodes.label: Opus 5 default Opus model
nodes.rationale: 2.1.219 added Claude Opus 5 (`claude-opus-5`) as the default Opus model, with a 1M context window and fast mode at $10/$50 per Mtok. The same release removed Opus 4.7 from fast mode (leaving Opus 5 and Opus 4.8), and 2.1.251 made Opus 5 the default for seat-based Enterprise subscriptions.

nodes.label: Sonnet 5 as the default model
nodes.rationale: 2.1.197 introduced Claude Sonnet 5 as the default model in Claude Code with a native 1M-token context window and promotional pricing of $2/$10 per Mtok through August 31. By 2.1.243 the picker and the bundled claude-api skill were updated to present $2/$10 as Sonnet 5's standard list price rather than a promo, and 2.1.247 changed its auto-compact window to the full 1M (compacting at ~967K instead of ~934K tokens).

nodes.label: 1M context windows and their enforcement
nodes.rationale: 1M context started as a paid extra, became default for Opus 4.6 on Max/Team/Enterprise at 2.1.75, and is native on Fable 5, Sonnet 5 and Opus 5. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT` (added 2.1.50) was widened at 2.1.223 from a fixed model list to every Claude model with a native 1M window, holding them to 200K via auto-compaction with a startup warning when that is not holding. The `[1m]` model-ID suffix caused recurring bugs: doubled suffixes (2.1.172), and Fable 5 suffixes now stripped automatically (2.1.173).

nodes.label: Reasoning effort levels and their reversals
nodes.rationale: `/effort` was added at 2.1.76. The level set reversed twice: 2.1.72 simplified effort to low/medium/high and REMOVED max; 2.1.111 then added `xhigh` for Opus 4.7 sitting between high and max, and later releases reference max again plus `ultracode`. Defaults also moved repeatedly — 2.1.94 raised the default from medium to high for API-key, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, Team and Enterprise; 2.1.117 set high for Pro/Max on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6; 2.1.68 set Opus 4.6 back to medium for Max and Team; 2.1.154 shipped Opus 4.8 defaulting to high.

nodes.label: Effort scope: session vs saved default
nodes.rationale: 2.1.251 changed `/effort` to save the chosen level per model, so each model keeps its own setting when switching. 2.1.257 added `s` in `/effort` to change effort for the current session only, matching `/model`, and changed `--effort` to lift a new model's default-effort hold for that session only rather than permanently.

nodes.label: Fast mode
nodes.rationale: Fast mode arrived for Opus 4.6 at 2.1.36. 2.1.142 moved its default to Opus 4.7 (with `CLAUDE_CODE_OPUS_4_6_FAST_MODE_OVERRIDE=1` to pin 4.6); that override was deprecated at 2.1.154 and made a no-op at 2.1.160. 2.1.154 repriced fast mode on Opus 4.8 to 2x the standard rate for 2.5x the speed, and 2.1.219 removed Opus 4.7 from fast mode so `/fast` applies to Opus 5 and Opus 4.8.

nodes.label: Extended thinking controls
nodes.rationale: Thinking is toggled by keyword (`think`/`think harder`/`ultrathink`, 0.2.44) and by a key that moved from Tab to Alt+T at 2.0.72. `DISABLE_INTERLEAVED_THINKING` was added at 1.0.1; thinking became default-on for Opus 4.5 at 2.0.67; 2.1.166 made `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0`, `--thinking disabled` and the per-model toggle actually disable thinking on models that think by default. 2.1.89 stopped generating thinking summaries by default in interactive sessions (`showThinkingSummaries: true` restores them).

nodes.label: Effort xhigh/max conflicts with thinking disabled
nodes.rationale: Combining a very high effort level with thinking turned off produced API errors: 2.1.221 fixed WebSearch failing with a 400 at effort xhigh/max when thinking is disabled, 2.1.243 improved the error to name the level and the disabling setting and suggest `/effort high`, and 2.1.251 fixed Opus 5 requests failing with 'effort ... is not supported when thinking is disabled' by sending effort as `high` in that case.

nodes.label: Permission modes
nodes.rationale: Claude Code's modes are default/manual, acceptEdits, plan, auto and bypassPermissions, cycled with Shift+Tab. 2.1.200 renamed the 'default' mode to 'Manual' across the CLI, `--help`, VS Code and JetBrains while still accepting `default`. 2.1.257 made `defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` in project `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json` be ignored (as `"auto"` already was); it must be set in user or managed settings or passed as `--permission-mode`.

nodes.label: Auto mode's progressive de-gating
nodes.rationale: Auto mode shipped behind flags and lost them one at a time: 2.1.111 removed the `--enable-auto-mode` requirement, 2.1.152 removed the opt-in consent, 2.1.158 made it available on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry behind `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1`, and 2.1.207 removed that opt-in too (disable via the `disableAutoMode` setting). 2.1.251 fixed the first launch on a fresh install starting in default mode instead of auto mode for accounts whose startup default is auto.

nodes.label: Auto-mode permission classifier
nodes.rationale: Auto mode adjudicates tool calls with an LLM classifier configured by `autoMode.allow`, `soft_deny`, `hard_deny` (2.1.136, unconditional blocks) and `environment` rules, where including `"$defaults"` adds custom rules alongside the built-ins instead of replacing them (2.1.118). `autoMode.classifyAllShell` (2.1.193) routes every Bash/PowerShell command through it. 2.1.210 defaulted the classifier to Sonnet 5 for external sessions, pinned per session; 2.1.246 added an Auto mode tab to `/permissions` for viewing and editing classifier rules.

nodes.label: Auto-mode safety rules
nodes.rationale: Auto mode carries named hard rules that grew over time: 2.1.183 blocks destructive git (`git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- .`, `git clean -fd`, `git stash drop`), `git commit --amend` on commits the agent did not make, and terraform/pulumi/cdk destroy unless the specific stack was requested; 2.1.205 added a rule blocking tampering with session transcript files and asks before `rm -rf` on an unresolvable variable; 2.1.257 added a Containment Escape rule so cloud metadata-credential fetches, egress evasion and cross-tenant reach are not auto-approved unless the environment marks them expected.

nodes.label: Permission rule syntax
nodes.rationale: Rules are `Tool(pattern)` strings in settings.json. 2.1.0 added `*` wildcards at any position (`Bash(npm *)`, `Bash(git * main)`); 2.1.178 added `Tool(param:value)` matching on a tool's input parameters (e.g. `Agent(model:opus)`); 2.1.166 allowed globs in the deny tool-name position (`"*"` denies all tools). 2.1.214 narrowed single-segment `dir/**` allow rules like `Edit(src/**)` to `<cwd>/dir` only, and 2.1.246 warns at startup about Bash allow rules with a wildcard before the subcommand (e.g. `Bash(git * main)`) because they also match inserted options.

nodes.label: Bash permission-check hardening
nodes.rationale: The Bash permission analyzer is the single largest recurring security surface: fixes cover prefix-matching bypass (1.0.120), shell line continuation (2.1.6), wildcard rules matching compound commands (2.1.7), heredoc delimiter smuggling (2.1.38), backslash-escaped flags (2.1.98), zsh `[[ ]]` regex conditionals (2.1.221), commands over 10,000 characters now always prompting (2.1.214), file-descriptor redirect forms failing closed (2.1.214), arithmetic assignments like `OPTIND=1/0` (2.1.252), and dangling `&&`/`||` operators (2.1.246). The stated design bias is to fail closed and prompt.

nodes.label: Input-redirect permission checking, reverted then re-landed
nodes.rationale: 2.1.232 made Bash input redirections (`< file`) permission-checked like their argument spellings on all platforms and tightened Cygwin-style symlink handling on Windows. 2.1.233 REVERTED both, stating a narrower version would return in a later release. 2.1.257 re-landed the narrower form: Bash `Read()`/`Edit()` deny rules now apply to `< file` redirects and reader commands like `tac` and `egrep`, so a deny rule on any argument or redirect target refuses the command.

nodes.label: PowerShell tool on Windows
nodes.rationale: A dedicated PowerShell tool shipped as an opt-in Windows preview at 2.1.84, rolled out progressively at 2.1.111 behind `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL`, and became default-on for Windows Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry users at 2.1.143 (with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`). 2.1.120 removed the Git for Windows requirement — when Git Bash is absent Claude Code uses PowerShell as the shell tool. It carries its own permission-bypass fixes (trailing `&` background jobs, `cd..`/`X:` built-ins, quoted paths, invisible Unicode).

nodes.label: Bash sandbox
nodes.rationale: Sandbox mode for the Bash tool was released for Linux and macOS at 2.0.24 and grew a `sandbox.*` settings tree: `filesystem.allowWrite`/`denyRead`/`allowRead`/`disabled`, `network.allowedDomains`/`deniedDomains`/`strictAllowlist`, `failIfUnavailable`, `bwrapPath`/`socatPath`/`ripgrep`, `allowAppleEvents`, `enableWeakerNetworkIsolation` and `allowUnsandboxedCommands`. 2.1.78 turned a silent sandbox disable (enabled but dependencies missing) into a visible startup warning.

nodes.label: Sandbox credential masking
nodes.rationale: 2.1.187 added `sandbox.credentials` to block sandboxed commands from reading credential files and secret environment variables. 2.1.221 added `mode: "mask"` on Linux/WSL, where sandboxed commands read a sentinel copy while the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on egress (macOS falls back to `deny`). 2.1.224 added `extract`, `onExtractNoMatch`, `decode: "jwt"` with `maskClaims`, and `awsPairs`/`sigv4` re-signing; these require `network.tlsTerminate` and are honored only from user, managed or `--settings` sources.

nodes.label: Hooks system
nodes.rationale: Hooks were released at 1.0.38 after community input on issue #712. They receive JSON on stdin and can block by exiting 2 or returning a decision object. Configuration grew per-command `timeout` (1.0.41), `once: true` (2.1.0), a conditional `if` field using permission-rule syntax (2.1.85), exec-form `args: string[]` that skips the shell (2.1.139), and `terminalSequence` output for notifications without a controlling terminal (2.1.141). 2.1.139 also made hooks run without terminal access so they cannot corrupt an on-screen prompt.

nodes.label: Hook event catalogue growth
nodes.rationale: Events accumulated release by release: Stop split into Stop and SubagentStop (1.0.41), PreCompact (1.0.48), UserPromptSubmit (1.0.54), SessionStart (1.0.62), SessionEnd (1.0.85), SubagentStart (2.0.43), PermissionRequest (2.0.45), prompt-based stop hooks (2.0.30), TeammateIdle and TaskCompleted (2.1.33), ConfigChange (2.1.49), WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove (2.1.50), Setup (2.1.10), PermissionDenied (2.1.89), StopFailure (2.1.78), PostCompact (2.1.76), CwdChanged and FileChanged (2.1.83), TaskCreated (2.1.84), InstructionsLoaded (2.1.69), Elicitation/ElicitationResult (2.1.76), MessageDisplay (2.1.152), DirectoryAdded (2.1.219), and PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch (2.1.251).

nodes.label: Hooks cannot outrank deny rules
nodes.rationale: A repeated class of fix establishes that hooks may tighten but not loosen permissions. 2.1.77 fixed PreToolUse hooks returning `"allow"` bypassing `deny` rules including enterprise managed settings; 2.1.101 fixed `permissions.deny` not overriding a hook's `permissionDecision: "ask"`; 2.1.110 re-checks a `PermissionRequest` hook's `updatedInput` against deny rules and makes `setMode:'bypassPermissions'` respect `disableBypassPermissionsMode`; 2.1.211 floors auto mode at a prompt when a PreToolUse hook says `ask`; 2.1.222 fixed PreToolUse auto-allow hooks bypassing tool restrictions in background agent tasks.

nodes.label: Custom subagents
nodes.rationale: Custom subagents arrived at 1.0.60 via `/agents` and `.claude/agents/*.md`. Frontmatter accreted `model` (1.0.64), `permissionMode` (2.0.43), `disallowedTools` (2.0.30), `memory` scope (2.1.33), `isolation: worktree` (2.1.50), `background: true` (2.1.49), `hooks` (2.1.0), `effort`/`maxTurns` (2.1.78), `initialPrompt` (2.1.83) and `experimental.cacheTtl` (2.1.248). 2.1.198 REMOVED the `/agents` wizard, directing users to ask Claude or edit `.claude/agents/` directly.

nodes.label: Subagent nesting depth reversed twice
nodes.rationale: Nested subagent spawning changed direction twice. 2.1.172 allowed sub-agents to spawn their own sub-agents up to 5 levels deep. 2.1.217 reversed that, making subagents no longer spawn nested subagents by default, with `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH` to allow deeper nesting. 2.1.219 settled on depth 3 by default (explicitly noted as 'was 1'), with `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH=1` to disable nesting.

nodes.label: Per-session subagent cap added then removed
nodes.rationale: 2.1.212 added a per-session cap of 200 subagent spawns (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION`, reset by `/clear`) to stop runaway delegation loops. 2.1.224 REMOVED that 200-subagent-per-session spawn cap so long-running sessions no longer refuse new agents, while keeping the separate concurrency cap (default 20, `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`, added 2.1.217) and the depth limits.

nodes.label: Subagents run in the background by default
nodes.rationale: 2.1.198 made subagents run in the background by default (previously a gradual rollout), so Claude keeps working while they run and is notified when they finish. 2.1.232 turned subagent forking on by default — a `subagent_type: "fork"` subagent inherits the full conversation and prompt cache — and made non-teammate agent spawns in interactive sessions run in the background by default. 2.1.218 made skills with `context: fork` run in the background too, opt-out per skill with `background: false`.

nodes.label: Subagent model resolution order
nodes.rationale: 2.1.251 REVERSED the precedence of `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`: it now sets the DEFAULT subagent model rather than overriding everything, so an agent definition's `model:` and an explicit per-spawn model take precedence over it. 2.1.257 then added `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE` to restore the old behaviour deliberately — applying `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` (or the main model) to every subagent and ignoring per-spawn and agent-definition overrides.

nodes.label: Agent teams
nodes.rationale: Agent teams shipped as a token-intensive research preview at 2.1.32 behind `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`, spawning teammates into tmux or iTerm2 panes (`teammateMode: "iterm2"`, 2.1.186). 2.1.178 REMOVED the `TeamCreate` and `TeamDelete` tools: every session now has one implicit team and teammates are spawned directly with the Agent tool's `name` parameter, with `team_name` accepted but ignored. 2.1.234 removed the 'Default teammate model' setting — teammates use the leader's model unless the spawn names one.

nodes.label: Cross-session messaging (SendMessage / ListAgents)
nodes.rationale: 2.1.224 added cross-session `SendMessage` with `ListAgents` discovery on macOS and Linux; 2.1.239 brought it to Windows; 2.1.248 extended it to Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and telemetry-disabled sessions. 2.1.232 added `@`-mentioning another session by name and unique session names per machine. Delivery semantics were hardened: refusals and dropped messages are reported to the sender rather than silently succeeding (2.1.238), and `notify_when_idle` (2.1.236) asks a peer for one idle notice with no polling.

nodes.label: Relayed agent messages carry no user authority
nodes.rationale: 2.1.166 hardened cross-session messaging so messages relayed via `SendMessage` from other Claude sessions no longer carry user authority: receivers refuse relayed permission requests and auto mode blocks them. 2.1.198 restated the rule for subagents — they treat messages from the agent that launched them as normal task direction, but an agent's message is still never treated as the user's approval. 2.1.205 made background task notifications explicitly state that no human input has occurred, preventing fabricated in-transcript approvals from being acted on.

nodes.label: Background sessions and the background daemon
nodes.rationale: Background agents began at 2.0.60 and grew into full background SESSIONS served by a daemon: `claude --bg`, `/background`, `←`-detach, and subcommands `attach`, `logs`, `stop`, `respawn`, `rm` (surfaced in `claude --help` at 2.1.251). A large share of every recent release is daemon reliability — version skew across auto-updates, stale `daemon.lock` PID reuse, sleep/wake clock jumps, retire→wake flag preservation, worktree locks and idle reaping.

nodes.label: Agent view (`claude agents`)
nodes.rationale: 2.1.139 added agent view as a research preview: `claude agents` lists every Claude Code session — running, blocked on you, or done — grouped as Needs input / Working / Completed. It gained `--json` for scripting (2.1.145) with `waitingFor`, `id`, `state` and `--all` fields, dispatch flags (`--add-dir`, `--settings`, `--mcp-config`, `--plugin-dir`, `--permission-mode`, `--model`, `--effort`, `--cwd`), `! <command>` shell sessions (2.1.154), pinned sessions via Ctrl+T (2.1.147), and PR links on rows.

nodes.label: Dynamic workflows
nodes.rationale: 2.1.154 introduced dynamic workflows: Claude authors a workflow that orchestrates work across tens to hundreds of background agents, viewed with `/workflows`. 2.1.202 added an advisory 'Dynamic workflow size' guideline in `/config` (not an enforced cap) plus `workflow.run_id`/`workflow.name` OTel attributes; 2.1.219 made medium (aim for fewer than 15 agents) the default and added the `workflowSizeGuideline` settings key. Workflow scripts run in a sandbox — 2.1.223 fixed dynamic `import()` escaping it.

nodes.label: Workflow trigger keyword renamed to `ultracode`
nodes.rationale: The prompt keyword that launches a dynamic workflow moved: 2.1.157 added a `/config` setting to stop the word 'workflow' from triggering one, 2.1.160 renamed the trigger keyword from `workflow` to `ultracode` (highlighted violet in the prompt input), and 2.1.178 narrowed the remaining trigger to explicit phrases like 'run a workflow' or 'workflow:' rather than any mention of the word.

nodes.label: Workflow tool prompt footprint cut
nodes.rationale: 2.1.248 cut the Workflow tool's description from about 5.7k tokens to about 1k by moving the script-writing reference into a bundled `workflow-authoring` skill that is loaded on demand. This is the same pattern applied to the bundled `claude-api` skill at 2.1.234, whose context cost dropped from ~200k+ tokens to ~25k by loading reference docs on demand.

nodes.label: Task and todo tooling
nodes.rationale: A Todo list arrived at 0.2.93; 2.1.16 replaced it with a task management system supporting dependency tracking (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=false` kept the old one temporarily). 2.1.233 then REMOVED the todo/task tracking tools (TaskCreate/Get/Update/List, TodoWrite) on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5 and newer models, with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` to bring them back — an explicit judgement that newer models do not need them.

nodes.label: `/goal` completion conditions
nodes.rationale: 2.1.139 added `/goal`: set a completion condition and Claude keeps working across turns until it is met, in interactive, `-p` and Remote Control, with a live elapsed/turns/tokens overlay. Its idle behaviour was tuned repeatedly — 2.1.234 checks in when background tasks keep a goal waiting 30+ minutes (`CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES=0` opts out), 2.1.239 backs the repeats off to 30 min, 1 h, then every 2 h, and 2.1.246 caps idle check-ins at three per goal until your next message. 2.1.234 also made `/goal` clear itself with a notice when a turn dies on an unrecoverable error instead of staying armed.

nodes.label: `/loop` recurring prompts
nodes.rationale: 2.1.71 added `/loop` to run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. `/loop 5m check the deploy`) plus cron scheduling tools for recurring prompts within a session; 2.1.105 made `/proactive` an alias. 2.1.248 made self-paced dynamic mode and the no-prompt autonomous default always available including on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, and 2.1.243 added a Loops breakdown to `/usage` (per-loop run count, tokens, tokens per run, last run) so runaway loops are easy to spot.

nodes.label: Plugin system and marketplaces
nodes.rationale: 2.0.12 released the plugin system: plugins ship commands, agents, skills, hooks, MCP and LSP servers from marketplaces, managed with `/plugin install|enable|disable|marketplace|validate` and repository-level `extraKnownMarketplaces`. Later additions include `claude plugin details`/`list`/`prune`/`tag`/`init`, `defaultEnabled: false` (2.1.154), plugin dependency resolution with version pins, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`/`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` variables, `bin/` executables (2.1.91), and `manifest.userConfig` options with keychain-stored `sensitive: true` values (2.1.83).

nodes.label: Plugin marketplace source types
nodes.rationale: Marketplace sources widened from github/git to `git-subdir` (2.1.69), npm with custom registries and version pinning (2.1.51), `source: 'settings'` inline entries (2.1.80), `archive` zip-over-HTTPS with optional SHA-256 pinning (2.1.224), and `command` sources where a local command prints the plugin directory and is re-resolved each session (2.1.229). 2.1.232 added GitLab support so bare `gitlab.com` repo URLs clone like `github.com` ones.

nodes.label: Plugin and marketplace governance
nodes.rationale: Admins constrain plugins through `strictKnownMarketplaces` (with `hostPattern`, `pathPattern` and `owner/*` wildcards), `blockedMarketplaces`, `pluginSuggestionMarketplaces`, `allowedChannelPlugins`, `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` and `pluginTrustMessage`. Enforcement was extended to install, update, refresh and autoupdate at 2.1.117, and hardened against escapes: 2.1.251 rejects marketplace-declared command paths outside the plugin directory, and 2.1.257 refuses any declared component path that is a symlink.

nodes.label: Claude Skills
nodes.rationale: Skills shipped at 2.0.20 as `SKILL.md` files under `.claude/skills/`. 2.1.0 added automatic hot-reload and `context: fork` execution in a forked sub-agent; 2.1.178 made nested `.claude/skills` directories load when working on files there, disambiguating name clashes as `<dir>:<name>`. Frontmatter accepts `allowed-tools`, `disallowed-tools` (2.1.152), `effort` (2.1.80), `agent`, `paths:` glob lists, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, and `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`/`${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}`/`${CLAUDE_EFFORT}` substitutions.

nodes.label: Skill listing description budget
nodes.rationale: The per-skill description cap in the listing moved in both directions: 2.1.86 capped `/skills` descriptions at 250 characters to reduce context usage, 2.1.105 raised the listing cap from 250 to 1,536 characters and added a startup warning when descriptions are truncated, and 2.1.32 made the skill character budget scale with the context window (2% of context) so larger windows show more descriptions. 2.1.144 moved the truncation warning out of startup and into `/doctor`.

nodes.label: Slash commands merged with skills
nodes.rationale: Custom slash commands began as markdown files in `.claude/commands/` at 0.2.31 with subdirectory namespacing (`/frontend:component`). 2.1.3 merged slash commands and skills into one mental model with no behaviour change, and 2.1.108 let the model discover and invoke built-in slash commands like `/init`, `/review` and `/security-review` through the Skill tool. 2.1.199 made stacked invocations like `/skill-a /skill-b do XYZ` load all leading skills, up to 5.

nodes.label: Bundled skills shipped with the CLI
nodes.rationale: Claude Code bundles first-party skills: `/claude-api` (2.1.69, later gaining `upgrade`, `cost-optimize`, `prompt-audit` subcommands and Admin API coverage), `/dataviz` (2.1.198), `/less-permission-prompts` (2.1.111), `/team-onboarding` (2.1.101), `/powerup` (2.1.90), `workflow-authoring` (2.1.248) and `/buddy` (2.1.89, April 1st). `disableBundledSkills` and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS` (2.1.169) hide bundled skills, workflows and built-in slash commands from the model.

nodes.label: `/code-review` and its renames
nodes.rationale: `/simplify` was renamed to `/code-review` at 2.1.147, reporting correctness bugs at a chosen effort level with `--comment` to post inline GitHub PR comments; the old cleanup-and-fix behaviour was removed, then re-created at 2.1.154 as a cleanup-only `/simplify`. 2.1.152 added `--fix` to apply findings. 2.1.223 made `/review` an alias of `/code-review` and made a bare invocation reuse the last effort level typed. 2.1.218 moved it into a background subagent, and 2.1.257 posts findings on GitLab merge requests via `glab mr note`.

nodes.label: `/ultrareview` cloud multi-agent review
nodes.rationale: 2.1.111 added `/ultrareview` for comprehensive code review in the cloud using parallel multi-agent analysis and critique, reviewing the current branch or a fetched GitHub PR. 2.1.120 added a non-interactive `claude ultrareview [target]` subcommand for CI that prints findings to stdout (`--json`) and exits 0 or 1. It seeds the cloud session from the local checkout, and 2.1.248 fixed it uploading uncommitted `prod.env`-style, `*.tfvars` and editor swap/backup copies of credential files.

nodes.label: Claude stops self-invoking heavyweight commands
nodes.rationale: A deliberate reversal of model autonomy: 2.1.215 stopped Claude running the `/verify` and `/code-review` skills on its own, requiring explicit invocation, and 2.1.218 changed `/deep-research` to start only when invoked manually. This runs against 2.1.246, which lets Claude start `/code-review` on its own on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, the apps gateway and telemetry-disabled setups — so the restriction is about unprompted invocation, not about which providers may use it.

nodes.label: MCP transports and config scopes
nodes.rationale: MCP support grew from stdio to SSE (0.2.54), streamable HTTP (1.0.27) and WebSocket. Scopes were renamed at 0.2.49 (old 'project' became 'local', 'global' became 'user') and 0.2.50 introduced the committable project-scope `.mcp.json`. Servers can be added by wizard, JSON string, or imported from Claude Desktop; `--mcp-config` accepts multiple files (1.0.73). Timeouts are governed by `MCP_TIMEOUT`, `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, per-server `timeout`/`request_timeout_ms`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT`.

nodes.label: MCP OAuth
nodes.rationale: Remote MCP servers gained OAuth at 1.0.27, Authorization Server discovery at 1.0.35, RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata discovery at 2.1.85, and Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD / SEP-991) support at 2.1.81 for servers without Dynamic Client Registration. `claude mcp login <name>` / `logout` (2.1.186) authenticate without the interactive menu, with `--no-browser` for SSH. Recurring failure modes fixed include concurrent-refresh races overwriting tokens, keychain corruption from large metadata blobs, and step-up `403 insufficient_scope` re-consent.

nodes.label: MCP tool search and deferral
nodes.rationale: 2.1.7 enabled MCP tool search auto mode for all users: when MCP tool descriptions exceed 10% of the context window they are deferred and discovered via the MCPSearch tool instead of being loaded upfront, disabled by adding `MCPSearch` to `disallowedTools`. 2.1.9 added `auto:N` to set that context-percentage threshold and 2.1.121 added a per-server `alwaysLoad` that exempts a server's tools from deferral. 2.1.119 disabled tool search by default on Vertex AI to avoid an unsupported beta header (opt in with `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`), re-enabled for 4.5-generation models at 2.1.221.

nodes.label: Managed MCP allow/deny policy
nodes.rationale: 2.0.22 added enterprise managed MCP allowlist and denylist support (`allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers`), later joined by `managed-mcp.json`, `allowAllClaudeAiMcps` (2.1.149) and `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`. Enforcement gaps were closed repeatedly: `--mcp-config` bypassing policy (2.1.83), agent-frontmatter MCP servers ignoring it (2.1.153), reconnect and IDE-typed configs (2.1.169), and `/mcp` reconnect/enable still connecting a settings-file server that a late-loaded policy should block (2.1.257).

nodes.label: MCP elicitation
nodes.rationale: 2.1.76 added MCP elicitation support, letting MCP servers request structured input mid-task through an interactive dialog of form fields or a browser URL, together with new `Elicitation` and `ElicitationResult` hooks that can intercept and override responses before they are sent back to the server.

nodes.label: MCP `headersHelper` dynamic auth
nodes.rationale: `headersHelper` (1.0.119) runs a command that mints HTTP headers for an MCP server, and was extended to plugin marketplaces at 2.1.238. It is treated as executable trust: 2.1.238 requires the folder's trust dialog for a project `.mcp.json` helper and strips inherited credential env vars, 2.1.207 rejects `${user_config.*}` in shell-form commands as a shell-injection fix, and 2.1.193 re-runs the helper and reconnects automatically on a 401/403.

nodes.label: Enterprise managed settings
nodes.rationale: Enterprise managed settings arrived at 2.0.68 and expanded into a policy tier: macOS plist and Windows Registry sources (2.1.51), a `managed-settings.d/` drop-in directory merging alphabetically (2.1.83), server-delivered remote settings with `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` failing closed (2.1.92), `requiredMinimumVersion`/`requiredMaximumVersion` (2.1.163), `parentSettingsBehavior` (2.1.133) and `managedSourcesBehavior: "merge"` (2.1.257). The Windows path moved from `C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode` to `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode`, deprecated at 2.1.2 and removed at 2.1.75.

nodes.label: Managed-settings security approval dialog
nodes.rationale: Server-managed settings that change security posture require the user's approval before applying. 2.1.232 made the dialog show endpoint URLs and require approval for sandbox binary overrides; 2.1.248 stopped benign client-timeout, MCP startup-mode and stream-watchdog env vars from triggering it; 2.1.251 added approval for settings that terminate sandbox TLS, route traffic through a proxy, inject credentials or weaken isolation, and for `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` setting credential/routing headers; 2.1.252 lists only the settings that changed since the last approval.

nodes.label: Organization model governance
nodes.rationale: Organizations constrain model choice via `availableModels`, tightened by `enforceAvailableModels` (2.1.175) so the allowlist also constrains the Default model and user or project settings cannot widen a managed list. 2.1.196 added org default models shown as 'Org default' in `/model`; 2.1.73 added `modelOverrides` mapping picker entries to provider IDs like Bedrock inference-profile ARNs; 2.1.243 added `modelPicker` (curate the picker) and `modelPricing` (use contracted rates for `/cost`, status line and telemetry instead of list price).

nodes.label: Third-party provider matrix
nodes.rationale: Beyond the first-party API, Claude Code runs on Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry (2.0.45), Bedrock powered by Mantle (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE=1`, 2.1.94) and Claude Platform on AWS (2.1.198). A recurring release pattern is bringing a feature already shipped on the Claude API to these providers — auto mode, `/loop`, `/radio`, `/code-review` self-start, cross-session messaging, the fullscreen renderer offer, session recap and streaming tool execution were each separately enabled on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry and telemetry-disabled setups.

nodes.label: Claude apps gateway
nodes.rationale: A Claude apps gateway fronts upstream providers with its own sign-in, failover chain, spend metering and spend limits (surfaced in `/usage` and as a `rate_limits.spend_limit` status-line field at 2.1.251). Gateway `/v1/models` discovery for the `/model` picker was automatic in 2.1.126–2.1.128 and then made OPT-IN via `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1` at 2.1.129. 2.1.257 made gateway sign-in and token refresh verify the gateway's pinned TLS certificate and added `forward_user_identity` for per-user spend attribution.

nodes.label: Credential isolation between hosts and subprocesses
nodes.rationale: A repeated fix class keeps each credential on its own host. 2.1.246 stopped telemetry and metrics requests to Anthropic carrying the API key configured for a third-party gateway — a credential is now only sent to its own host. 2.1.257 fixed doubly-listed `Authorization` headers overriding configured credentials on Bedrock/Mantle/Vertex/WIF, stray host headers reaching Foundry/Vertex/Bedrock, and a leftover Anthropic key being sent alongside a Foundry subscription key. `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1` (2.1.83) strips Anthropic and cloud credentials from Bash, hook and MCP subprocess environments.

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry instrumentation
nodes.rationale: Claude Code emits OTel metrics, logs and traces covering token/cost usage, `tool_decision`, `tool_result`, `user_prompt`, `api_request`/`api_error`, `skill_activated`, `at_mention`, `pull_request.count`, `active_time.total`, and interaction/LLM/tool spans with `agent_id`/`parent_agent_id`/`workflow.run_id` attributes. 2.1.193 added `claude_code.assistant_response` carrying model response text, redacted unless `OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES=1` — and warned that when unset it follows `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS`, so deployments already logging prompts start receiving response content on upgrade.

nodes.label: Remote Control
nodes.rationale: Remote Control bridges a local terminal session to claude.ai/code so it can be driven from web or phone; `/remote-control` and `claude remote-control` (2.1.51 for external builds) manage it, with a footer pill replacing the startup banner at 2.1.162. It is disabled when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a non-Anthropic host (2.1.196) and when an API key or `apiKeyHelper` is set (2.1.139). 2.1.222 made repo-local settings able to turn it OFF but never ON — that must be user scope. 2.1.257 fixed dismissing its consent prompt counting as consent.

nodes.label: Cloud sessions and teleport
nodes.rationale: Claude Code runs sessions in the cloud for web, desktop and mobile, seeded from a local checkout and reachable back on the CLI with `claude --teleport <session id>` (2.0.24). Supporting pieces are `/web-setup` GitHub connection, `--from-pr` (2.1.27), `/remote-env`, cloud environments auto-created on demand (2.1.101), and a session network proxy that applies the environment's allowed domains to Bash and other tools (2.1.239). 2.1.257 made reading an artifact that is not yours always ask first in Cowork and claude.ai cloud sessions, even in auto mode.

nodes.label: Self-hosted runner
nodes.rationale: 2.1.224 added self-hosted environments: `claude self-hosted-runner` turns your own machines or containers into a place Claude Code web, mobile and desktop sessions can run, on Team and Enterprise plans. Flags added since include `--client-label` (2.1.248), `--defer-shutdown-max-min` and `--proxy-authorization-command`/`--proxy-authorization-file` for egress proxies needing a fresh header per connection (2.1.238), a required `--base-dir` on Windows (2.1.229), and `--configure-git` push negotiation (2.1.257).

nodes.label: Scheduled tasks and routines
nodes.rationale: In-session cron tools (`CronCreate`/`CronList`) arrived with `/loop` at 2.1.71, disabled mid-session by `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON` (2.1.72), with `--resume`/`--continue` resurrecting unexpired scheduled tasks (2.1.110). A `ScheduleWakeup` tool and cloud `/schedule` routines followed. 2.1.183 fixed scheduled-task and webhook deliveries being treated as keyboard input: they now classify as task notifications and can no longer approve a pending action or set the session title in auto mode.

nodes.label: Prompt caching
nodes.rationale: Prompt-cache hit rate is treated as a first-class metric, with dozens of fixes for cache busts caused by tool schemas changing mid-session, OAuth token refresh re-rendering tool definitions, date in the system prompt, MCP `instructions` connecting late, and resume re-injecting the skill listing. Controls include `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` / `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M` (2.1.108), `promptCacheTtl` and `subagentPromptCacheTtl` settings (2.1.243), and per-agent `experimental.cacheTtl` frontmatter (2.1.248). 2.1.251 added a per-session prompt-cache line to `/cost` and a `prompt_cache` status-line object.

nodes.label: Conversation compaction
nodes.rationale: Automatic compaction for effectively unbounded conversations arrived at 0.2.47; its warning threshold moved from 60% to 80% at 1.0.51 and compaction became instant at 2.0.64. Failure modes were bounded rather than retried forever: 2.1.76 added a circuit breaker stopping after 3 consecutive failures, 2.1.89 detects a thrash loop where context refills immediately after three compactions and stops with an actionable error, and 2.1.142 seeds the first summarize attempt from the original overflow size instead of wasting a near-full retry. PreCompact (1.0.48) can block compaction and PostCompact (2.1.76) fires after.

nodes.label: Usage, cost and context visibility
nodes.rationale: `/context` (1.0.86) shows what fills the window and gained actionable optimization suggestions at 2.1.74. 2.1.118 merged `/cost` and `/stats` into `/usage`, which added a per-category breakdown of what drives limits — skills, subagents, plugins and per-MCP-server cost (2.1.149) — plus a Loops breakdown (2.1.243) and a Spend limit bar (2.1.251). Status-line JSON exposes `context_window`, `current_usage`, `rate_limits`, `effort.level`, `thinking.enabled`, `prompt_cache` and `workspace.git_worktree`.

nodes.label: Memory and auto-memory
nodes.rationale: 2.1.32 made Claude automatically record and recall memories as it works, managed with `/memory` (2.1.59). Memory files carry last-modified and ISO `modified` frontmatter timestamps so Claude can reason about freshness. The `MEMORY.md` index is bounded — 200 lines and 25KB (2.1.83) — with 2.1.210 turning an over-limit write into an explicit error instead of silent truncation. `autoMemoryDirectory` (2.1.74) relocates storage and `CLAUDE_MEMORY_STORES` mounts team memory stores.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md and rules loading
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md gained `@path/to/file.md` imports at 0.2.107 and `.claude/rules/*.md` (with `paths:` frontmatter for conditional loading) at 2.0.64. 2.1.72 changed HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`) to be hidden from Claude when auto-injected while staying visible to the Read tool. 2.1.169 made the 'CLAUDE.md is too long' warning threshold scale with the model's context window, and 2.1.206 added a `/doctor` check proposing to trim checked-in CLAUDE.md content Claude could derive from the codebase itself.

nodes.label: Git worktree isolation
nodes.rationale: `--worktree` / `-w` (2.1.49) starts a session in an isolated git worktree; `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` tools switch mid-session and agents declare `isolation: "worktree"`. Isolation is enforced against escapes rather than assumed: fixes cover `git -C`/`--git-dir`/`GIT_DIR` redirection (2.1.216), destructive git against the main checkout (2.1.222), committed `.claude/worktrees` symlinks (2.1.212), and Windows NTFS junctions. `worktree.sparsePaths` (2.1.76) and `worktree.bgIsolation: "none"` (2.1.143) tune it.

nodes.label: Worktree base ref reversed
nodes.rationale: The branch point for new worktrees flipped and then became configurable. 2.1.128 changed `EnterWorktree` to create the new branch from local HEAD as documented instead of `origin/<default-branch>`, so unpushed commits were no longer dropped. 2.1.133 added the `worktree.baseRef` setting (`fresh` | `head`) and explicitly noted that its default `fresh` changes `EnterWorktree`'s base BACK to `origin/<default>`; `worktree.baseRef: "head"` keeps unpushed commits in new worktrees.

nodes.label: Native binary distribution
nodes.rationale: 2.1.113 changed the CLI to spawn a native Claude Code binary via a per-platform optional dependency instead of bundled JavaScript, with npm installs deprecated at 2.1.15. Size and memory then became a recurring line item: zstd compression cut the Linux x64 download from about 340 MB to 75 MB (2.1.243), on-demand code loading saved roughly 40–70 MB per session, dropping six rarely used syntax-highlighting languages saved 2.5 MB (2.1.251), and 2.1.252 cut a further ~5 MB.

nodes.label: Embedded search replaces Glob and Grep on native builds
nodes.rationale: 2.1.117 replaced the `Glob` and `Grep` tools on native macOS and Linux builds with embedded `bfs` and `ugrep` reachable through the Bash tool, giving faster searches without a separate tool round-trip; Windows and npm-installed builds were unchanged. 2.1.162 made explicitly listing Grep/Glob in `--tools` restore the dedicated search tools on those builds, where the names had previously been silently ignored.

nodes.label: Reduced-capability launch modes
nodes.rationale: Several flags strip Claude Code down for different reasons. `--bare` (2.1.81) skips hooks, LSP, plugin sync and skill walks for scripted `-p` calls and requires an API key. `--safe-mode` / `CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE` (2.1.169) disables all customizations for troubleshooting. `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE` (2.1.50) strips skills, memory, agents, MCP, hooks and CLAUDE.md. `--restricted` / `CLAUDE_CODE_RESTRICTED=1` (2.1.248) is the security-shaped one: it removes command- and code-executing built-in tools and WebFetch, confines file tools to the working directory, refuses `bypassPermissions`, and ignores user, project and local settings files.

nodes.label: Headless mode and the Agent SDK
nodes.rationale: Print mode (`-p`) gained `--output-format=stream-json` at 0.2.66, structured output via `--json-schema` and the `StructuredOutput` tool, `--include-partial-messages` (1.0.109), `--forward-subagent-text` with nested-subagent forwarding (2.1.211/2.1.219), `--max-budget-usd` (2.0.28) and `--max-turns`. The TypeScript and Python SDKs shipped at 1.0.23; 2.0.0 renamed the Claude Code SDK to the Claude Agent SDK and 2.0.25 removed the legacy entrypoint in favour of `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`.

nodes.label: Fullscreen (flicker-free) renderer
nodes.rationale: The alt-screen renderer arrived as `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1` at 2.1.89, became switchable in-session with `/tui fullscreen` and a `tui` setting at 2.1.110, and was offered by a one-time prompt on new installs (extended to Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry at 2.1.239). It brings virtualized scrollback, mouse support and copy-on-select; `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1` (2.1.132) opts out, and 2.1.236 made a failed start fall back to the classic renderer instead of exiting on every launch.

nodes.label: Screen reader and accessibility mode
nodes.rationale: 2.1.208 added an opt-in screen reader mode with plain-text rendering, via `claude --ax-screen-reader`, `CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1`, or `"axScreenReader": true`. Follow-ups announce deleted text for word and line deletions (2.1.218), hide decorative glyphs and read nested tables as `Header: value.` lines (2.1.200), announce permission mode changes on Shift+Tab (2.1.210), render `/effort` as a numbered list (2.1.233), and keep the native terminal cursor on the focused row so magnifiers can follow. 2.1.236 added VS Code transcript announcements.

nodes.label: Customizable keybindings
nodes.rationale: 2.1.18 added customizable keyboard shortcuts configured per context in `~/.claude/keybindings.json`, including chord sequences, via `/keybindings`. 2.1.238 added `keybindingFlavor: "readline"` making Ctrl+W delete back to whitespace as in Bash (default `"classic"` unchanged), extended at 2.1.239 to Alt+F/Alt+D word semantics. 2.1.246 made an unknown action name skip rather than deaden the key. 2.1.257 added an `Agents` context so `claude agents` Ctrl+G/Ctrl+S/Ctrl+T are rebindable.

nodes.label: Claude in Chrome
nodes.rationale: Claude in Chrome shipped as a beta at 2.0.72 (browser control from Claude Code via the Chrome extension) and became generally available at 2.1.198. Sessions get isolated Chrome tab groups closed on `/clear` and exit (2.1.239), a `/chrome` browser picker (2.1.154), and hardened file-upload path validation. 2.1.251 routed browser actions through Claude Code's own permission checks even in telemetry-disabled sessions, which previously used the extension's own prompts.

nodes.label: Read-before-edit and file tool rules
nodes.rationale: The rule that Edit requires a prior Read was loosened stepwise: 2.1.89 accepted `sed -n`/`cat` views, 2.1.144 accepted `head`/`tail`, and 2.1.160 accepted single-file `grep`/`egrep`/`fgrep`. 2.1.228 went further and let NEWER models overwrite an existing file with Write without having read it this session, matching Edit's rules, while older models still require the read. Read itself gained a `pages` parameter for PDFs (2.1.30) and returns a truncated 'PARTIAL view' page instead of a hard error on oversized reads (2.1.145).

nodes.label: WebSearch and WebFetch
nodes.rationale: A web fetch tool arrived at 0.2.53 and web search at 0.2.105. WebFetch identifies itself as `Claude-User` so operators can allowlist it via robots.txt (2.1.83), strips `<style>`/`<script>` before conversion (2.1.105), caches URLs for 15 minutes (`CLAUDE_CODE_WEBFETCH_CACHE_TTL_MS`, 2.1.233), and saves binary responses to disk. 2.1.212 added a session-wide WebSearch cap of 200 calls (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION`) to stop runaway search loops.

nodes.label: AskUserQuestion behaviour
nodes.rationale: An interactive question tool arrived at 2.0.21, with a '(Recommended)' indicator and the recommended option moved to the top at 2.0.62. 2.1.154 told Claude to reserve the multiple-choice prompt for decisions it genuinely cannot make itself. 2.1.200 changed `AskUserQuestion` dialogs to no longer auto-continue by default, with an opt-in idle timeout in `/config`. 2.1.85 let PreToolUse hooks satisfy it by returning `updatedInput` with `permissionDecision: "allow"`, enabling headless integrations that collect answers in their own UI.

nodes.label: EndConversation tool
nodes.rationale: 2.1.214 added the EndConversation tool, letting Claude end sessions with highly abusive users or jailbreak attempts, matching behaviour claude.ai has had since 2025 and citing https://www.anthropic.com/research/end-subset-conversations.

nodes.label: SendFeedback tool
nodes.rationale: 2.1.247 added the SendFeedback tool: when something goes wrong in a session Claude can draft a feedback report for the user to review and send from `/feedback`, turned off with the `feedbackDrafts` setting. It complements the session quality survey whose sample rate enterprise admins set via `feedbackSurveyRate` (2.1.76).

nodes.label: Monitor tool
nodes.rationale: 2.1.98 added the Monitor tool for streaming events from background scripts, with plugins able to declare background `monitors` that auto-arm at session start or on skill invoke (2.1.105). 2.1.236 set Monitor allow rules aside while auto mode is active so Monitor commands are reviewed like Bash commands, and 2.1.257 made `claude -p` wait for an armed Monitor to fire or time out instead of exiting about 5 seconds after its final result.

nodes.label: Output styles deprecated then un-deprecated
nodes.rationale: Output styles shipped at 1.0.81 with built-in 'Explanatory' and 'Learning' styles. 2.0.30 DEPRECATED them, pointing users at `--system-prompt-file`, CLAUDE.md and plugins; 2.0.32 UN-DEPRECATED them based on community feedback. 2.1.73 then deprecated only the `/output-style` command in favour of `/config`, fixing the style at session start for better prompt caching. A built-in 'Concise' style was added at 2.1.237.

nodes.label: Spend caps and usage credits
nodes.rationale: `--max-budget-usd` was added at 2.0.28 and made to actually halt background subagents at 2.1.217: once the cap is reached new spawns are denied and running background agents are stopped. 'Extra usage' was renamed to 'usage credits' at 2.1.144 (`/extra-usage` became `/usage-credits`), with admin-request flows for Team and Enterprise, and gateway spend limits surfaced in the usage warning at 2.1.225. `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG` fails immediately on org spend-limit and out-of-credits errors rather than waiting for a reset (2.1.239).

nodes.label: Commit and PR attribution
nodes.rationale: 2.0.60 added the model name to `Co-Authored-By` commit trailers; 2.0.62 added an `attribution` setting customizing commit and PR bylines, deprecating `includeCoAuthoredBy`; 2.1.183 added `attribution.sessionUrl` to omit the claude.ai session link from commits and PRs in web and Remote Control sessions. 2.1.251 changed the default trailer to `Co-Authored-By: Claude Code` when the active model is not a recognized Claude model, e.g. a third-party model behind a custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`.

nodes.label: Stream watchdog, retries and non-streaming fallback
nodes.rationale: A streaming idle watchdog aborts and retries when a response produces no events; 2.1.196 turned it on by default for all providers (`CLAUDE_ENABLE_STREAM_WATCHDOG=0` disables, `CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` sets the threshold, default 90s at 2.1.84). Retry policy is layered: transient 429s and ECONNRESET retry with backoff, `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES` was capped at 15 at 2.1.186 with `CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG` for unattended sessions, and a non-streaming fallback exists with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONSTREAMING_FALLBACK` to turn it off. 2.1.111 REVERTED the 2.1.110 cap on non-streaming fallback retries because it traded long waits for outright failures.

nodes.label: Automatic continuation of cut-off responses
nodes.rationale: Rather than surfacing a partial answer as an error, Claude Code now resumes: 2.1.0 continues automatically when a response is cut off by the output-token limit, 2.1.199 preserves partials from a mid-stream overloaded error with an incomplete-response notice, 2.1.246 auto-continues non-interactive (`-p`, SDK, cloud) responses cut off by a server error, connection loss or stall, and 2.1.257 extends the same behaviour to subagents cut off by computer sleep, a dropped connection or a server error.

nodes.label: Symlink and path-traversal hardening
nodes.rationale: Symlinks and unusual path spellings are a persistent escape vector. Fixes include writing new files through a symlinked parent in acceptEdits mode (2.1.69), allow rules checking the resolved target (2.1.89), `/rewind` refusing to restore through symlinks or hard links (2.1.216), Grep/Glob applying `Read()` deny rules through symlinked search paths (2.1.251), file tools following a symlink swapped in AFTER the permission check (2.1.251), background session directories not canonicalized (2.1.217), and Windows NT-namespace `\??\` paths bypassing UNC validation and leaking NTLM credentials (2.1.233 and 2.1.234).

nodes.label: Workspace trust
nodes.rationale: A directory must be trusted before repo-resident configuration can execute. 2.1.51 fixed `statusLine` and `fileSuggestion` hook commands running without trust; 2.1.69 fixed the trust dialog silently enabling all `.mcp.json` servers on first run; 2.1.196 stopped `claude mcp list`/`get` spawning self-approved `.mcp.json` servers, showing `⏸ Pending approval` instead; 2.1.218 required an agent file's own folder to be trusted before its frontmatter hooks run; 2.1.232 stopped nested git repositories inheriting trust from a parent directory.

nodes.label: Project settings lose privileged keys
nodes.rationale: A steady direction of travel strips authority from repo-committed `.claude/settings.json`, because a checked-in file is attacker-controllable. 2.1.207 stopped auto mode reading `autoMode` from `.claude/settings.local.json` and stopped plugin option values being read from project settings; 2.1.222 stopped repo-local settings turning Remote Control ON (they may still turn it off); 2.1.232 restricted `sandbox.ripgrep` to user/managed/`--settings`; 2.1.251 stopped project `env` setting `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR` or `TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP`, and blocked project settings enabling detailed beta tracing or raw API body logging; 2.1.257 ignores a project `defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"`.

nodes.label: Long-session memory and performance campaign
nodes.rationale: Unbounded growth in long sessions is one of the changelog's largest recurring themes, with dozens of named leaks fixed: MCP stdio stderr accumulating up to 64 MB per server, LSP documents held open (now LRU-capped at 50), tree-sitter WASM heap never shrinking, React `memoCache` retaining old message arrays, truncated MCP outputs keeping the full result, subagent tool results held past the display window, and transcript-wide tool lookups copied per rendered row. Structural fixes bound rather than trim: tool results over 50K characters persist to disk (2.1.51), and transcript size dropped up to 79x in edit-heavy sessions by pruning superseded file-history backups (2.1.208).

nodes.label: `/doctor` as the diagnostics surface
nodes.rationale: `/doctor` became the destination for warnings pulled out of startup: 2.1.205 turned it into a full setup checkup that can diagnose and fix issues, with `/checkup` as an alias and `f` to have Claude fix reported issues (2.1.105). It now reports unreachable permission rules, MCP schema errors and cross-scope conflicts, plugin advisories and skipped auto-updates, externally managed launchers, server-managed settings load failures (2.1.248), skill-listing truncation, and stale sandbox mask files (2.1.257) — a deliberate move of noise out of the launch path.

nodes.label: IDE extensions (VS Code and JetBrains)
nodes.rationale: 2.0.0 shipped a new native VS Code extension, tracked in the changelog under a `[VSCode]` prefix with its own feature line: session groups and archiving in the sidebar, a Focus view hiding tool activity behind per-turn summaries, native `/mcp` and `/context` dialogs, plan preview documents with comments, Remote Control controls, screen-reader announcements, and a model pill with an effort row (2.1.257). JetBrains appears mainly through rendering and synchronized-output fixes.

nodes.label: LSP tool
nodes.rationale: 2.0.74 added an LSP tool giving go-to-definition, find-references and hover documentation through language servers, which plugins can supply and declare in `.lsp.json`. It gained `startupTimeout` (2.1.50), `clientInfo` identification (2.1.98), a working `workspaceSymbol` query parameter (2.1.162), zombie-server restart on next request (2.1.89), and filtering of results from gitignored directories (2.1.47).

nodes.label: Documented behaviour reversals
nodes.rationale: The changelog explicitly reverses its own prior decisions often enough to be a pattern, and the reversals are stated rather than silent: output styles deprecated then un-deprecated, subagent nesting enabled then disabled then re-enabled at a lower depth, a 200-subagent session cap added then removed, gateway model discovery automatic then opt-in, `EnterWorktree`'s base ref flipped then made configurable back, `< file` redirect checking landed then reverted then narrowed, `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` demoted from override to default then given a `_FORCE` companion, and the non-streaming fallback retry cap reverted one release after it shipped. 2.1.212 even carries an explicit correction of an earlier release note (2.1.200, about tmux synchronized output).
